hook.text: In fission, a neutron strikes a uranium-235 nucleus—which absorbs it, becomes unstable, and splits into two.

buildup.text: The split releases 2–3 new neutrons plus enormous energy—about 200 million electron-volts per fission event.

discovery.text: Those freed neutrons can hit other U-235 atoms—triggering more fissions in a self-sustaining chain reaction.

twist.text: Without control, the chain reaction multiplies in microseconds—that's how a nuclear bomb works.

climax.text: Reactors use control rods to absorb excess neutrons—keeping the chain reaction steady, not explosive.

punchline.text: One neutron splits one atom—and the chain begins.

quiz.question: What sustains a nuclear chain reaction?
options: Neutrons released by each fission event
